notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached, and no hardware or sim-engine run is claimed. The card's entry_symbols list is empty, so there was no symbol to verify; the card's five model files exist in the clone. The package serves the card's models[0], autobio/model/hand/dexhand021_right.xml, as a configuration-only MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [12 numbers]}}; each ctrl element is checked by the bridge against the model's explicit actuator_ctrlrange (twelve position actuators, model:208-220) before data.ctrl is written, then mj_step runs ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed), with 19 qpos and 19 qvel values from the model's 19 hinge joints. The served model step is the MJCF's own 0.01 s (model:5). The other card models (the three shadow-hand models and the vortex mixer) are not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0]. The vortex mixer model is also not self-contained for the real engine because it uses the mjlab.passive.detent plugin (model/instrument/vortex_mixer_genie_2.xml:39-43), while the served dexhand model is a standalone MJCF with its mesh assets present in the clone.

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver and the upstream provides MJCF simulation assets rather than a single device class, so there is no deviation from the card. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the class FakeMujoco; driver.lock.json names it .fake:FakeMujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF for the 19 joints, the twelve actuators, their explicit control ranges and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each directly actuated joint toward its control target. It has no transmission model, so the five tendon actuators move no joint; it loads no STL mesh and resolves no contact, equality, damping, armature or actuator-force constraint. The fidelity gaps list every difference. The model file is read from the read-only clone in place; the package copies neither the model nor its STL assets, and it does not import or run upstream code.

WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface to check; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which the authoring guide's expected-warning list calls expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds seven cases (model shape from the card model, control-vector length, control-range refusal with zero effect, step advancing the integration state, reset to the model defaults, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no operator-required bound and no driver-declared Limit is present; the control envelope is derived from the model at run time.
